article.title: No Rookie QBs to Start NFL Week 1 for Just Second Time in 19 Seasons
article.summary: For the 2026 NFL season, no rookie quarterbacks are slated to start in Week 1, marking only the second instance of such an occurrence in the last 19 seasons. This rare development sees top draft picks Fernando Mendoza of the Las Vegas Raiders and Ty Simpson...

article.content_html:
Key Developments

The 2026 NFL season opener will feature a rare sight: no rookie quarterbacks starting under center. This marks only the second time in the past 19 seasons that all first-year signal-callers will begin the season on the bench. The decision by the Las Vegas Raiders to keep No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza as a reserve behind veteran Kirk Cousins is particularly notable, especially given the recent trend of top draft picks immediately taking the field.

Mendoza is the first No. 1 overall quarterback selection to start his career as a backup since Baker Mayfield in 2018. Following Mayfield, the subsequent six No. 1 overall picks all earned Week 1 starting jobs. Mayfield himself eventually made his first start in Week 4 after coming in as a reserve in Week 3. Alongside Mendoza, the Los Angeles Rams' No. 13 overall pick, Ty Simpson, will also start the season as a reserve, contributing to this unusual statistic.

The last time no rookie quarterback started Week 1 was in 2022, a season where Kenny Pickett was the sole first-round quarterback, drafted 20th overall by Pittsburgh. Prior to that, the only other instance in the last 19 seasons occurred in 2007. That year, JaMarcus Russell, the No. 1 overall pick by the Raiders, held out through the summer and did not sign his contract until after the season opener, making his first start in the final game of that season.

This trend goes against the recent shift in NFL strategy, where teams have increasingly been quicker to hand the reins to young quarterbacks. In three of the previous five seasons, three rookie quarterbacks started the opener, reflecting a perceived narrowing gap between college and professional football. Historically, 20 of the 30 quarterbacks taken first overall since the common draft era began in 1967 started their season opener as rookies. All but one of these No. 1 picks, Carson Palmer in 2003, made at least one start in their inaugural year.

Key Takeaways

  • No rookie quarterbacks are slated to start Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season, a rare occurrence seen only once before in the last 19 seasons (2022).
  • Las Vegas Raiders' No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and Los Angeles Rams' No. 13 pick Ty Simpson will both begin their careers as reserves.
  • Mendoza is the first No. 1 overall quarterback since Baker Mayfield (2018) to start his rookie season on the bench, contrasting a recent trend of immediate starts for top picks.

Why It Matters

This development signals a potential, albeit temporary, shift in how NFL teams are approaching the integration of their top rookie quarterbacks. For years, the league has seen a growing inclination to throw highly drafted signal-callers directly into starting roles, driven by the belief that immediate experience accelerates development and that the college-to-pro transition is less daunting. The decision to bench both the No. 1 overall pick and another high first-rounder suggests a renewed emphasis on patient development, allowing young talents like Mendoza and Simpson to learn the professional game without the immediate pressure of Week 1 starts. This could reflect a strategic choice by certain franchises to prioritize veteran leadership and a more gradual acclimatization process, potentially influencing future draft and development strategies across the league.
